body:
Looks like we need to specify `ecmaVersion: 6` in addition to `sourceType: "module"` in escope in order for that to work. 

Workaround for now: either enable `ecmaFeatures.blockBindings` or the `es6` environment.
the second .eslintrc example above is using the `es6` environment and still failing, right?

Sorry, I missed that. The key thing is `blockBindings` , so can you try just using that with `modules` and see what happens?

Was an error message output above what you pasted? Looks like you may have copied just under the actual message.

I'm mobile for the rest of the day, so sorry I can't do much debugging myself.
ok, found the issue... the code is checking for an attribute called `module` (singular) and I am using `modules` (plural) on my .eslintrc

Similar thing happens with exports:

```
D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\node_modules\estraverse\estraverse.js:517
                        throw new Error('Unknown node type ' + nodeType + '.')
                              ^
Error: Unknown node type ExportDefaultDeclaration.
    at Controller.traverse (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\node_modules\estraverse\estraverse.js:517:31)
    at EventEmitter.module.exports.api.verify (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\eslint.js:706:24)
    at processFile (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli-engine.js:193:27)
    at D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli-engine.js:293:26
    at walk (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:81:9)
    at D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:102:9
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at traverse (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:101:11)
    at CLIEngine.executeOnFiles (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli-engine.js:284:9)
    at Object.cli.execute (D:\Projects\Web\eBookTracker\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli.js:178:65)
```

If I remove "modules" from ecmaFeatures then there's no exception.

using `ecmaFeatures.module` I no longer get the throw, and the output is:

```
test.js
  1:1  error  Illegal import declaration

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

is that the expected output for the javascript code of the original report?
I was originally using `modules` based on this recommendation https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1944#issuecomment-77707309

workaround: use both module and modules ;)

I can send a PR to fix the check and expect only modules in the plural

Actually, you are right: using both module and modules fixes import exception in one file, but it doesn't fix export exception from my report above. @nzakas, should I submit a separate bug report or you can use this one for both exceptions?
@extesy please for a separate issue for that.
